enriched_problems.nature: phishing attacks leveraging website impersonation and malicious redirects
enriched_problems.description: Phishing attacks in the web security domain exploit website impersonation and malicious redirect techniques to deceive users into divulging sensitive credentials. These attacks often involve crafting HTML content that mimics legitimate websites, embedding social engineering cues, and using sophisticated URL structures to bypass detection. The large-scale, text-heavy, and HTML-structured nature of the data reflects real-world phishing campaigns that combine multi-modal features such as embedded scripts, suspicious redirects, and credential harvesting forms. These attacks are designed to exploit user trust and browser vulnerabilities, posing significant risks to individuals and organizations.

real_world_context.domain_insights: Analysis of the kpd dataset reveals phishing websites that use complex HTML DOM structures with embedded scripts and deceptive URL patterns to impersonate legitimate domains and redirect users to credential harvesting pages.
real_world_context.attack_sophistication: Attacks range from basic copycat phishing pages to advanced multi-stage redirects and dynamic content injection, reflecting evolving attacker tactics to evade traditional detection.
real_world_context.technical_implementation: Phishing pages utilize crafted HTML with embedded forms mimicking legitimate login portals, combined with URL obfuscation and redirect chains to mask the final malicious destination, often leveraging social engineering text content to increase user trust.
real_world_context.threat_landscape: Phishing remains a prevalent and evolving threat within web security, with attackers increasingly using multi-modal content and sophisticated URL manipulation to bypass detection systems.
real_world_context.victim_impact: Victims typically suffer credential compromise leading to unauthorized access, financial loss, identity theft, and erosion of trust in online services.

detection_criteria: Deviation from normal pattern analysis in HTML structure and URL composition
Presence of suspicious redirects and credential harvesting forms
Text content exhibiting social engineering language
normal_vs_malicious: Normal pages exhibit consistent HTML DOM patterns and stable URL structures
Malicious pages show abnormal redirects, obfuscated URLs, and embedded deceptive forms
measurable_thresholds: Thresholds on redirect chain length exceeding normal baselines
Frequency of suspicious keywords in text content above typical benign levels
HTML script complexity metrics deviating from legitimate sites

attack_scenarios: A phishing site mimics a popular bank login page using identical HTML structure but includes hidden form fields to capture credentials.
A malicious URL uses multiple redirects starting from a seemingly benign domain to a credential harvesting page with embedded social engineering text.
A phishing webpage embeds obfuscated JavaScript that dynamically alters the DOM to evade static pattern detection.
legitimate_scenarios: A legitimate e-commerce website with stable URL structure and consistent HTML layout serving product pages.
A corporate intranet portal with secure login forms and no redirect chains.
A news website with high text content volume but no embedded credential forms or suspicious redirects.

risk_reduction: Implement URL filtering to detect and block suspicious redirect chains
Deploy HTML content analysis focusing on form authenticity and script behavior
Educate users on recognizing social engineering cues embedded in web content
Use multi-modal detection combining URL, HTML, and text content analysis based on identified patterns
Continuously monitor baseline web traffic patterns to identify anomalies indicative of phishing

diversity_dimensions: Varying attack sophistication levels from simple impersonation to advanced redirects

Multi-stage URL redirects to mask final malicious destination

threat_intelligence.current_threat_landscape: Phishing attacks remain a dominant threat in web security, with attackers increasingly leveraging sophisticated website impersonation and multi-stage redirects to evade detection and harvest credentials.
